_doc: Every label that holds a ticket out of a worker's queue, and the code that takes it out again (ASK-4011).
Founder, 2026-11-08: "We cannot have these things get stuck again on rules that are not being enforced and then tickets don't get done because they're waiting for someone that doesn't exist."

Read by q-system/.q-system/tests/test_hold_label_consumers.py (CI) and by q-system/.q-system/scripts/stall-sweep.py (com.kipi.stall-sweep, ASK-4019), which names the next consumer of every held ticket idle 24h.

`labels` must hold EXACTLY the labels linear-worker.sh ready() refuses, read from its source by AST, plus every `lane_holds` label. A new ready() refusal fails CI until it has a row here: the test is declared to the capability gate with no `covers`, so it runs on every PR, including one that only touches linear-worker.sh (PR #666 round 2). `lane_holds` is DECLARED, not discovered: each row's marker must exist in its path, but a new lane refusal is caught only when its author adds the row (PR #666 review, minor). The census that cannot be fooled covers ready() only.
`refused_when`: `present` (the label holds the ticket) or `absent` (missing the label holds it, as with owner:sana).
Each row has exactly one of:

`consumer`: an in-repo script (`path`) whose source carries the label literal, run by a committed, non-retired com.kipi template (`job`) whose ProgramArguments reach the script, directly or through `via` (a `./kipi <verb>` case).

`outside_consumer`: code another repo owns (`repo`, `path`, `marker`, `job`, `owner`). Named, not verified here; that repo's own suite owns it. Its label must be in the test's OUTSIDE_ALLOWED, so adding one is a reviewed edit.
`missing`: no consumer exists yet. It names the ticket that builds one. The set of missing labels may only shrink: the test pins its ceiling.
A person is never a consumer. A row that names one is a missing row.

`caps`: a consumer that stops is not an exit. Every `*_CAP` constant the consumer's source defines is classified here, both directions, so a new cap fails CI until somebody says whether reaching it strands the ticket. `per_ticket: true` needs an `after_cap` ticket that builds the next consumer, and puts the label in the test's CAP_GAP_CEILING, which may only shrink. `per_ticket: false` needs a `what` (a batch bound strands nothing). PR #666 round 1, major 2: needs-scope read as covered while the drafter keeps the label ON at REDRAFT_CAP.
The census reads ready() at ANY depth: a refusal nested in an inner block, or reached through `not helper(i)`, is counted, and `not` inverts the polarity (PR #666 round 1, major 1).

consumer.what: Nightly at 02:00: any open fleet ticket with no owner:* label gets owner:sana and one comment naming its next consumer (ASK-4010).

missing.what: Nothing moves an owner:assaf ticket. ASK-3961 relabels the error-path ones owner:sana and lists the true spend, scope or reach questions for the founder in one place a job writes.

consumer.what: Nightly at 03:00: selects on the label, rewrites the DoR, drops the label so ready() offers it again, up to 3 redrafts.

REDRAFT_CAP.what: At 3 of 3 the drafter writes TERMINAL_NOTE and keeps needs-scope ON deliberately (linear-dor-drafter.py:1182-1193), so this consumer stops and ready() keeps refusing the ticket.

after_cap.what: Nothing selects on a capped needs-scope ticket. ASK-4092 builds the next consumer: a different strategy, a recorded reversible close, or an age sweep. Until it lands this label is in CAP_GAP_CEILING, which may only shrink.

PENDING_CAP.what: How many issues one nightly run drafts. A ticket over the batch bound is offered again the next night, so it strands nothing.

missing.what: Nothing re-tests the block, so the label never clears. ASK-3960 records a probe per ticket and re-runs it nightly.
lane_pool skips a held alert forever, and the hold keeps needs-triage, so chief's triage never reaches its park rule either. ASK-4014 builds the re-test.
